## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on the integral \(q^r\)-box Schur basis and integral Pieri rule, for \(p=c=1\), \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(d=ij\), and \(0\le k\le b:=\min(i,j)\), the degree-\(d+k\) columns are exactly
  \[
  P_{x,k-x}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},\,k-x)},\qquad 0\le x\le k,
  \]
  with a zero final part omitted. The requested target is established under these presentation hypotheses.

## Strategy
Let \(\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\) contain \(i^j\) and have \(|\mu|=d+k\). Its first \(j\) rows have lengths \(i\) or \(i+1\); partition order forces the \(i+1\)'s to occupy precisely the first \(x\) rows. Its only possible additional row has length \(y\). Hence
\[
\mu=((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)=P_{x,y},\qquad x+y=k.
\]
Conversely, for \(0\le x\le k\), \(x\le k\le j\) and \(k-x\le k\le i\), so \(P_{x,k-x}\) is in the box. This proves completeness.

Order these columns by
\[
C_x:=P_{x,k-x}\qquad(0\le x\le k).
\]
For \(0\le x\le k-1\), Pieri gives
\[
h_1P_{x,k-1-x}=P_{x+1,k-1-x}+P_{x,k-x}
=C_{x+1}+C_x.
\]
Both summands remain in the box because \(x+1\le k\le j\) and \(k-x\le i\). Thus the \(h_1\)-row lattice is the unsigned path-incidence lattice
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]

Retaining \(C_0\), delete its column. The row matrix on \((C_1,\ldots,C_k)\) is lower unitriangular, hence has determinant \(1\). Retaining \(C_k\), delete its column; on \((C_0,\ldots,C_{k-1})\) the matrix is upper unitriangular, again of determinant \(1\). Therefore either endpoint is retained by a unimodular complement. For \(k=0\), the row lattice is \(0\) and the empty complementary minor has determinant \(1\).

## Gaps
The argument assumes the stipulated integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation; that presentation is not independently proved here.

## Next
No broader quotient, all-degree, or minimality claim is made.
